baslik: The Airliner That Suddenly Dove Twice on Its Own

sahneler.metin: Cruising over Western Australia, an Airbus suddenly pitched down.
In seconds, unbelted passengers were thrown into the ceiling.
The pilots hadn't moved the controls.
One air data unit was sending short spikes of false data.
The flight computers read them as a stall and pushed the nose down.
The crew landed safely at a nearby air base.
Airbus then changed the software to reject spikes like these.

aciklama:
Qantas 72 pitched down violently twice in cruise. The cause: incorrect angle-of-attack spikes passed to flight control computers by a faulty ADIRU.
